construct: Biallelic GAA loss of function causes deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase, preventing normal lysosomal glycogen degradation. Glycogen accumulates within lysosomes, damaging cardiac and skeletal muscle.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Infantile hypotonia, feeding difficulty, macroglossia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and markedly reduced acid alpha-glucosidase activity identify infantile Pompe disease from lysosomal glycogen accumulation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Danon disease is a legitimate infantile cardiomyopathy/lysosomal alternative, but the measured acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency is specific for Pompe disease. McArdle, von Gierke, and SMA do not fit the combined enzyme and cardiomyopathy phenotype.
